structure: Part 2 of Confluence page "Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields - V4", version 210 (no page-level status macro, so nothing here rests on an unapproved decision). Read in full: rows 14 to 31 of the single 8-column table in the h2 section 'Live Animal Data Elements' (ac:local-id 2e90e927-5a96-4a60-a08c-1856a37cde30), i.e. from the place_of_origin row to the end of the table, plus the two expand macros nested in those rows' cells. The table's columns, read from its header row (claimed by part 1), are: Field Name | Type | Conditions / Values | Applies at: | Source | Mandatory | Example | Impacts. The 18 rows covered, in page order: place_of_origin (Place of Origin), consignor (Consignor), consignee (Consignee), importer (Importer), place_of_destination (Place of destination), permanent_address (Permanent Address), transporter_type (Transporter type), commercial_transporter (Commercial Transporter), private_transporter (Private Transporter), county_parish_holding_cph (County Parish Holding (CPH)), port_of_entry (Port of Entry), arrival_date_at_port (Arrival date at Port), means_of_transport (Means of transport), transport_identification (Transport identification), transport_document_reference (Transport document reference), transited_countries (Transited Countries), and two consecutive rows both labelled 'Contact Address' that both carry the one anchor contact_address (the first sourced from gov.identity, the second user-created via the Standard address block). The slice ends at ; the next h1, 'Reason of Import', belongs to part 3. Two collapsed expand macros sit inside these rows and are read in full: 'Permanent address required commodities (3)' (3 entries, title count agrees) and 'CPH required commodities (19)' (19 entries, title count agrees). Both sit in the 'Applies at:' column cell of their row, not in the 'Conditions / Values' cell as the source scope says — recorded as a decision, and for permanent_address the expand occupies that cell instead of an 'Applies at' level, which is claimed as a gap. Nine of the 18 rows name the Standard Address Block as their Type (place_of_origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place_of_destination, permanent_address, commercial_transporter — address block plus approval number — private_transporter, and the second Contact Address row), so part 6's Address Block validation ties to them. The slice holds the page's one explicit TBC (commercial_transporter: 'consumed from TBC list that holds the approved transporters'), one row with three blank-or-'-' cells (the first Contact Address row: Type, Mandatory, Example), and three internal contradictions claimed as gaps (permanent_address's missing level, the duplicate contact_address anchor, and transited_countries being marked 'Applicable to Animals only' and 'Optional' while carrying a GERMINALS marker and a 'Conditional: required when...' bullet).

claims.statement: Nine fields in this half of the Live Animal Data Elements table name the Standard Address Block as their type, so the Address Block section's field-level validation governs all of them: Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination, Permanent Address, Commercial Transporter (address block plus approval number), Private Transporter and the user-created Contact Address.
